subject: Q3 readiness: executive summary, constraints & dependency handoff
messages:
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com, markus_klein@redwood.com, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
Cc: sarah@acme.com
Date: Sun, 23 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Q3 readiness: executive summary, constraints & dependency handoff

Team —

Attached is a compact snapshot of where we sit halfway through Q3 (see attachment: q3_okr_health_snapshot.xlsx). High-level summary up front:

- Platform latency & stability OKR (Owner: Markus) — 62% complete; several regression signals after last model roll; ongoing mitigation but we need extra GPU capacity for a two-week soak to validate quantized builds.
- Cost per 1k tokens (Owner: Laura) — 48% complete; current plans hit target only with aggressive batching; this will impact tail-latency for customer-facing routes.
- Customer reliability (Owner: Vanessa) — topline NPS is steady, but a key account (Acme Analytics) has flagged slowed inference for large-batch exports. This is an active renewal risk.

Primary asks:
1) Engineering runway: request +2 dedicated A100 weeks (or equivalent vCPUs/GPU hours) to soak the quantized 2.1 variant and finish kernel tuning.
2) Scoped rescope: propose reverting low-traffic experimental routes (alpha-prefetch) to v1 behavior for Q3 to free cache and reduce variance.
3) Sales/customer ops: Vanessa, can you surface the Acme renewal touchpoints and ask procurement for patience while we stabilize? I included Sarah (Acme) to keep them in the loop.

If we don't secure the extra capacity and accept the rescope, we expect to miss the cost-per-token target but preserve customer SLAs. If we don't rescope, we risk both SLA slips and higher cost. I recommend the conservative path unless product-level tradeoffs disagree.

Next steps: I propose a 30-min sync tomorrow at 11:00am PT to confirm owners and finalize the QBR dry run deck.

Attachments: q3_okr_health_snapshot.xlsx

Thanks —
Tessa Morgan
Head of Product Operations
Redwood Inference
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: tessa_morgan@redwood.com, markus_klein@redwood.com, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 23 Aug 2026 11:00:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Q3 readiness: executive summary, constraints & dependency handoff

Thanks, Tessa —

Read the snapshot. A couple quick clarifying items:

- On the cost OKR, can you call out which customer routes are most impacted by the batching change? If it's internal analytics/ingest vs. real-time API routes, that changes the tradeoff.
- For the proposed revert of alpha-prefetch, do we have a list of downstream teams that need to be notified (Search infra, Experimentation)? I want to avoid surprise rollbacks for product teams.

I agree the conservative path is reasonable, but we should also surface any quick wins (config tweaks, cache TTL changes) that could reduce the required extra capacity. If we can free up one week of GPU equivalent, that reduces the ask to a partial shift.

I'll be on tomorrow's 11:00am PT sync; assigning myself to help draft a 5-slide exec summary for the QBR dry run (ETA: EOD Monday).

Laura Bennett
Director, Product Management
Redwood Inference

From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
To: tessa_morgan@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Cc: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 23 Aug 2026 16:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Q3 readiness: executive summary, constraints & dependency handoff

Quick engineering note:

- The regression after the 2.1 rollout looks tied to one kernel path that degrades at >512 token context for the quantized path. We've got a patch that narrows the window, but it still needs a soak under real traffic to validate there are no tail regressions.
- Capacity ask: the two-week A100 soak is conservative; if we can do a staged soak (one full A100 for 4 weeks but with traffic mirroring) we can get statistically significant results and reduce burn. I attached a short plan (proposed_resource_shift.pdf) with options: 2-week full soak vs 4-week staged mirror.
- Risk tradeoff: reverting alpha-prefetch will reduce tail variance immediately and buys us 3 business days of headroom while the soak runs. Downsides: slightly higher token cost on the prefetched path and some lost telemetry for the experiment.

I can commit to leading the soak if we approve the staged mirror option. ETA to have the soak infra ready: Wed 08/26 if we greenlight capacity today.

-Markus
VP, Engineering (Serving Runtime)
Redwood Inference

Date: Mon, 24 Aug 2026 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Q3 readiness: executive summary, constraints & dependency handoff

Tessa / all —

Thanks for the clear note. Surface-level commercial implications: Acme (Sarah) is in the middle of renewal conversations and the slowdown on exports is already in the ticket queue. If we signal an ongoing outage or extended performance degradation during QBR, that materially increases churn risk.

Suggestions:
- Prioritize the customer-facing export route to keep Acme within SLA for large exports; move the experimental routes fallback first (this buys us fewer customer-facing impacts).
- I'll spin up a short joint note to Acme (Sarah) to set expectations and give them a tentative timeline; Sarah — can you confirm if a tentative 2-week stabilization window is acceptable?
- Procurement@bigco.com is copied for any contract-level levers if we need credits or a temporary SLA concession.

I agree with Markus on the staged mirror soak — lower total burn and faster validation of the kernel patch with less risk.

Vanessa Ortiz
Head of Customer Success
Redwood Inference

Thanks everyone — good alignment. Quick readout / action register to close this thread: 

Action items (owners & deadlines):
- Approve staged mirror soak (Markus) — decision + resource booking by EOD 24 Aug. (If approved, infra ETA Wed 08/26).
- Draft 5-slide exec summary for QBR dry run (Laura) — draft due EOD Mon 08/25.
- Customer comms to Acme (Vanessa + Sarah) — short note to set expectation and tentative 2-week stabilization window by Tue 08/25.
- Revert alpha-prefetch on low-traffic routes (Engineering lead to confirm list) — coordinated notification to downstream teams by Tue 08/25; temporary cost delta tracked in the QBR appendix.

I'll book the 11:00am PT slot for tomorrow and include a short pre-read (two slides) summarizing the decision points. If procurement/finance needs to approve credits or shifted budgets, we'll route that after we pick a soak option.

Attachments: proposed_resource_shift.pdf, q3_okr_health_snapshot.xlsx

Thanks —
Tessa Morgan
Head of Product Operations
Redwood Inference
